outcome: Intrusion prevention finally reaches the encrypted majority of traffic instead of only the shrinking unencrypted slice under a documented decryption policy.
overview: Government perimeter replacements are usually driven by end of support rather than by a capability gap, which makes the migration itself the whole engagement. Cisco Secure Firewall with Snort-based intrusion prevention is a common landing point where the estate is already Cisco-managed and the operations team knows the tooling. The design decision that carries the most weight is decryption: without it, intrusion prevention applies to a shrinking minority of traffic, and quoting throughput without it produces a device that cannot do the job it was bought for.

benefits.text: Intrusion prevention runs inline with an openly documented rule format
benefits.limits: Open rule format aids transparency and custom rules; it does not by itself make coverage better than a closed engine’s

benefits.text: The platform sits inside management tooling the operations team already uses
benefits.limits: Familiarity reduces operational risk during migration; it is not an argument about the platform’s security capability

benefits.text: One policy model covers appliance and virtual form factors as workloads move
benefits.limits: Policy is portable across form factors; throughput is not and must be re-sized with decryption enabled for each

residency: Appliances, management and logs remain inside the entity’s estate; no session content leaves the jurisdiction in this design

notFor.situation: An entity whose operations team has no existing familiarity with this vendor’s management tooling
notFor.why: The main operational argument for this platform disappears, and the choice should be made on capability alone

notFor.situation: A boundary where decryption is prohibited and traffic is overwhelmingly encrypted
notFor.why: Inline prevention would apply to a small minority of sessions, which is not what the investment is for

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Cisco security implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks depending on rule-base size and window availability
Support model: Vendor hardware and subscription support with a replacement term appropriate to government criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case.
1) Analyse — rule export, permissive-entry identification, traffic profiling with decryption impact measured
2) Design — decryption policy with exclusions, converted rule base, sizing at the enabled figure
3) Rehearse — cutover runbook validated with a rollback path
4) Cut over and hand over — migration in window, central management established, operations handed over
deliverables: Measured throughput under decryption and prevention meets the design figure
The decryption policy names, per category, what is inspected and what is excluded and why
Inspection decisions are logged with enough context for a rule review
